extracted.intended_audience: overseas researchers (foreign researchers) newly arrived in Japan and affiliated with Japanese universities/research institutions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for foreign researchers on eligibility, application procedures, allowable uses of funds, reporting, and selecting the appropriate Grants-in-Aid for Scientific Research (Kakenhi) category while affiliated with a Japanese research institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Researcher eligibility — engagement/affiliation
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) Be engaged in carrying out the subject research activities at the subject research institution. Be affiliated with the subject research institution in either a paid, unpaid, full-time or part-time capacity. (Researchers whose main duties at the subject institution are other than the subject research are also eligible.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must be affiliated with and engaged in the research at the host institution; employment can be paid or unpaid and full- or part-time. Confirm with the host institution's admin office whether your affiliation satisfies this requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Researcher eligibility — actual conduct of research
rubrics_metrics.description: (2) Be actually engaged in conducting the subject research at the subject research institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicant must physically and practically conduct the proposed research at the named institution (not just nominally affiliated). Ask the institution's admin office for interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution eligibility — implementation as institution project
rubrics_metrics.description: (3) After the grant is issued, the research institution must implement the subject research activity as its own project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The host institution must treat the funded activity as an institutional project (not purely a private award to an individual). Administrative acceptance by the institution is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution eligibility — administration of funds
rubrics_metrics.description: (4) The research institution must administer the grant money as its own funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The host institution is responsible for receiving, holding, and managing the grant; applicants cannot receive/handle funds personally. Consult the institution's admin office for fund-management procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choosing the appropriate grant category
rubrics_metrics.description: Various grant categories have been established to correspond with project objectives, funding scale, duration and other factors. Researchers may freely choose from among them the category that best coincides with their research plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the category that matches objectives, scale, and duration of your project. Refer to the English application guidelines/forms (FY2009 link provided) for category-specific rules and deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant application timing / frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: In each grant category, applications are received once a year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific deadlines differ by category; consult the application guidelines for the category you intend to apply for. (FY2009 English guidelines/forms linked.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Application language
rubrics_metrics.description: Yes. Application may be prepared in English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: English application guidelines and forms are provided (link cited for FY2009). Check the current year's guidance for updated English materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission route — via affiliated institution
rubrics_metrics.description: You must submit it via your affiliated research institution. You may not submit your application directly to JSPS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate with your host institution's admin office for internal deadlines and submission procedures; JSPS receives applications through institutions only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and selection timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Time frames differ by grant category as each has its own screening process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to application guidelines for category-specific selection schedules; contact institution admin for more concrete timetable information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start of research using grant funds
rubrics_metrics.description: You may start it as soon you receive your selection notice. (If your research continues for multiple years, you may start using each year’s grant from 1 April without interruption from the previous year.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not spend funds before selection notice. For concrete grant usage procedures, check with your institution's admin office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted uses of grant funds
rubrics_metrics.description: The grant is used to cover the cost of goods and services required for carrying out the subject research and to compile the research results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given: purchase equipment and materials, cover travel costs, pay remunerations. For concrete allowed expenditures and procedures, consult the institution's admin office and category-specific guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carry-over and intra-year budget adjustment rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant funds are to be expended by the end of each fiscal year of the funded project. Therefore, they may not freely be carried over into the next fiscal year. However, the four expense items in the grant application form may be freely adjusted up to 50% within each fiscal year. JSPS’s authorization must be obtained to adjust them more than 50%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unplanned carry-over to the next fiscal year is not permitted except in approved cases when scheduled research cannot be completed for unavoidable reasons; such carry-over requires procedures via the institution's admin office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct vs. indirect costs — definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct costs are those for goods and services required to carry out the subject research and to compile the research results, including purchasing equipment and materials, covering travel costs, and paying remunerations. Indirect costs are those involved in maintaining the environment required to implement the subject research, including personnel costs, facility maintenance, and library operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these definitions to classify budget items on the application; consult institutional finance/admin staff for accounting treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure if grantee returns home before grant period ends
rubrics_metrics.description: If you cannot continue your scheduled research because you intend to return early to your country, you must submit a report on the state of your grant expenditures and the results of your research to date. If unspent funds remain, you must return them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow your institution's instructions for reporting and returning funds; contact the admin office for the exact forms and timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting requirements during and after grant
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of a multi-year grant, a report is to be submitted at the end of each fiscal year on the state of your grant expenditures and research progress. Upon completion of the research, a report is to be submitted on the overall research results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult your institution's admin office for instructions on report preparation and filing (formats, deadlines). Annual and final reports are mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host institution administrative responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The admin office of your host institution in Japan is responsible for the overall administration of its Kakenhi program, including issuing calls for applications, providing selection notices, disbursing grants, and carrying out grant administrative procedures for both JSPS and the grantees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct inquiries about detailed procedures, deadlines, and interpretation of eligibility to your host institution's admin office; they act as the intermediary with JSPS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant categories — functions, typical duration and funding scale
rubrics_metrics.description:
Table of categories with intended functions, durations, and typical funding scales (as presented):
- Specially Promoted Research: Internationally appraised research expected to produce outstanding results; 3–5 years; 500 million yen or more per project.
- Scientific Research in Priority Areas: Highly responsive on issues of urgent societal needs that require global collaboration; 3–6 years; 20–600 million yen yearly per area (research in a proposed research area).
- Scientific Research on Innovative Areas: Joint research in new disciplines that contributes to elevating Japan's scientific standard and fostering young researchers; 5 years; 10–300 million yen yearly per area (research under a proposed research project).
- Scientific Research (Innovative/topical/leading-edge/creative): Various subcategories for innovative topical research and leading-edge research; examples include 3 years at 10 million yen yearly (Innovative Areas), 5 years at 50–200 million yen per project (leading-edge), and Scientific Research classes S/A/B/C with ranges [A]20–50M, [B]5–20M, [C]up to 5M over 3–5 years.
- Exploratory Research: Uniquely original research in an early stage; 1–3 years; up to 5 million yen per project.
- Grant-in-Aid for Young Scientists: Research team led by researcher up to age 42 (start-up) 5 years, 30–100 million yen per project; individual researcher up to age 37 (A)2–4 years 5–30M, (B) up to 5M; Start-up grants: 2 years, up to 1.5M per year.
- Encouragement of Scientists: Research by an employee of an educational or research institution or a corporation or any other individual; 1 year; up to 1 million yen.
- Grant-in-Aid for Special Purposes / Publication of Scientific Research Results: Support for publishing/disseminating significant research results, academic journals, compiling databases and opening them via scientific information networks.
- Other programs: Grant-in-Aid for JSPS Fellows (pre/postdoctoral, up to 3 years), Creative Scientific Research (advance selected components of highly creative research; 5 years), Specially Designated Research Promotion (support by MEXT), support for private research institutes to satisfy specific demands, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use category descriptions, durations, and funding scales to determine the best fit for your project. Refer to the official application guidelines for precise eligibility, scope, and application forms for each category and year (FY-specific differences exist). Contact your institution admin for advice on which category to pursue.
